decisions.claim: B expressed lack of concern or worry (likely about exams)
decisions.reason: Second-review support: Turn 9 'Oh, don't you?' is a tag-question reply-act that presupposes B made a negative statement of the form 'I don't [verb]' — most naturally 'I don't worry' or 'I don't care.' This is not merely inferring from A's exasperation; the grammatical structure of 'don't you?' directly echoes and presupposes B's prior negative utterance expressing lack of concern. The exam context from turn 7 ('You'll get exams next month') makes 'likely about exams' a reasonable connection, though the core claim (B expressed lack of concern) is firmly established by the reply-act implication.
